title: Psalm 43
opening_line: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause

source.note: Received text from the official Free Church digital edition and plain-text archive.

text.diplomatic: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause
text.normalized: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause
text.reading: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause

text.diplomatic: against th’ ungodly nation;
text.normalized: Against th’ ungodly nation;
text.reading: against th’ ungodly nation;

text.diplomatic: From the unjust and crafty man,
text.normalized: From the unjust and crafty man,
text.reading: From the unjust and crafty man,

text.diplomatic: O be thou my salvation.
text.normalized: O be thou my salvation.
text.reading: O be thou my salvation.

text.diplomatic: For thou the God art of my strength;
text.normalized: For thou the God art of my strength;
text.reading: For thou the God art of my strength;

text.diplomatic: why thrusts thou me thee fro’?
text.normalized: Why thrusts thou me thee fro’?
text.reading: why thrusts thou me thee fro’?

text.diplomatic: For th’ enemy’s opprëssion
text.normalized: For th’ enemy’s opprëssion
text.reading: For th’ enemy’s opprëssion

text.diplomatic: why do I mourning go?
text.normalized: Why do I mourning go?
text.reading: why do I mourning go?

text.diplomatic: O send thy light forth and thy truth;
text.normalized: O send thy light forth and thy truth;
text.reading: O send thy light forth and thy truth;

text.diplomatic: let them be guides to me,
text.normalized: Let them be guides to me,
text.reading: let them be guides to me,

text.diplomatic: And bring me to thine holy hill,
text.normalized: And bring me to thine holy hill,
text.reading: And bring me to thine holy hill,

text.diplomatic: ev’n where thy dwellings be.
text.normalized: Ev’n where thy dwellings be.
text.reading: ev’n where thy dwellings be.

text.diplomatic: Then will I to God’s altar go,
text.normalized: Then will I to God’s altar go,
text.reading: Then will I to God’s altar go,

text.diplomatic: to God my chiefest joy:
text.normalized: To God my chiefest joy:
text.reading: to God my chiefest joy:

text.diplomatic: Yea, God, my God, thy name to praise
text.normalized: Yea, God, my God, thy name to praise
text.reading: Yea, God, my God, thy name to praise

text.diplomatic: my harp I will employ.
text.normalized: My harp I will employ.
text.reading: my harp I will employ.

text.diplomatic: Why art thou then cast down, my soul?
text.normalized: Why art thou then cast down, my soul?
text.reading: Why art thou then cast down, my soul?

text.diplomatic: what should discourage thee?
text.normalized: What should discourage thee?
text.reading: what should discourage thee?

text.diplomatic: And why with vexing thoughts art thou
text.normalized: And why with vexing thoughts art thou
text.reading: And why with vexing thoughts art thou

text.diplomatic: disquieted in me?
text.normalized: Disquieted in me?
text.reading: disquieted in me?

text.diplomatic: Still trust in God; for him to praise
text.normalized: Still trust in God; for him to praise
text.reading: Still trust in God; for him to praise

text.diplomatic: good cause I yet shall have:
text.normalized: Good cause I yet shall have:
text.reading: good cause I yet shall have:

text.diplomatic: He of my count’nance is the health,
text.normalized: He of my count’nance is the health,
text.reading: He of my count’nance is the health,

text.diplomatic: my God that doth me save.
text.normalized: My God that doth me save.
text.reading: my God that doth me save.
